extraction.Name: Frank Twiss
extraction.Refused/Protested: did not want his patent to his 320 acre allotment at the time he got it, as he did not want to pay taxes; but the Indian Agency informed him that, if he did not take it over, the land would be assessed for taxes, sold for them, too; so he accepted the patent
extraction.Sold/Mortgaged: mortgaged his allotment to J.C. Jordan, of Gordon, Nebraska, for $150.00; that he never made this payment; that, in 1923, there being $150.00 more against the allotment in taxes, Jordan paid them, and foreclosed on the land
extraction.Buyer: J.C. Jordan, of Gordon, Nebraska; mortgage for $150.00; foreclosed in 1923; Jordan took the half section for himself
extraction.Tax burden forced sale/Mortgage: got behind in the taxes, and, in 1919, he mortgaged his allotment; in 1923, there being $150.00 more against the allotment in taxes, Jordan paid them, and foreclosed on the land
extraction.Occupation/Income: only income is what he can make by farm labor, this being his only income
extraction.NOTES: Mentally competent, has poor health, having stomach trouble; has a wife to support, and she has poor health, being bothered with rheumatism; has no children nor grandchildren to support; he empowered Jordan to sell one quarter of the land to pay off the mortgage and accumulated taxes, but Jordan took the half section for himself instead; deponent considers he got less than nothing for his allotment; has never received any help from the County, State nor the United States Government; document dated November 27, 1928
